project.name: Recall
project.description: A self-maintaining, vendor-neutral memory system. Three tiers: immutable episodic capture; a semantic consolidated tier (plaintext Markdown as source of truth plus a rebuildable SQLite index); and an offline consolidation loop that reconciles them via a confidence-gated split between a probabilistic LLM classifier (proposes) and a deterministic executor (writes). Product claim: never wrong silently, never loses ground truth, honest about its own measured error rate.
invariants: brain/ is the source of truth; brain/.brainindex/ (SQLite) is a gitignored, fully rebuildable index that must never hold anything not recoverable from the Markdown.
The episodic tier (brain/episodic/) is immutable and append-only; corrections are new captures that reference the old one, never mutations.
Expensive reasoning (LLM classification, consolidation) runs only at write-time / offline, never in the read/query path or a live session-start path.
The probabilistic classifier only proposes; the deterministic executor is the only thing that writes to the semantic tier. The LLM never both judges and acts.
Contradictions are never auto-applied and verification never auto-corrects; both only route to the review queue.

Conflict-classification accuracy has a measured ceiling (~65.3%, CONFLICTS benchmark, frontier models). Any classifier change must report its own measured accuracy on the real eval set, never an assumed one.
Recall reads AIW's tracked files read-only and never writes to .ai/; Recall's write path targets only brain/.
The data format is vendor-neutral plaintext + git and the classifier must stay provider-swappable (Anthropic is the current default, not a lock-in).

Dogfood Recall on its own build: before any recall-v1 task transitions to done, capture that task's non-obvious decisions / conflicts / owner corrections via 'recall capture'. A bad dogfood result is a finding to surface, not to hide. See .ai/decisions/0007.

recall-v1.title: Recall v1 — vendor-neutral plaintext memory with confidence-gated consolidation
recall-v1.objective: Carry BUILD_PLAN.md to a trustworthy, dogfoodable v1. Done: episodic+index round-trip, classifier eval (60.5% measured on 76 real cases), consolidation loop, retrieval+injection+provenance, correction loop, Phase 6 deterministic verification (partial). Remaining: CLI polish (recall status), close the provider-portability gap in the write path, add read-only AIW integration, and dogfood Recall's consolidation on this repo's own decision history.

aiw-readonly-integration.title: Read-only AIW consolidated-tier reader for a session-start hook
acceptance: A command (e.g. 'recall inject --for-session') reads only brain/semantic/ + the SQLite index and emits the injection-formatted context
That path makes zero network calls, zero model calls, and no writes anywhere; a test asserts this
Measured wall time < 150ms on a brain/ with ~100 facts; recorded in the test or an eval note
Documented boundary in .ai/decisions/0006 or a code comment: Recall never writes .ai/
constraints: Invariant 3 + 7: cheap local read only, never writes .ai/, never in an expensive path
Does not add a Recall hook to .claude/ or .codex/ in this task — just the readable command

combined-corruption-rate.title: End-to-end silent-corruption rate: classifier gate + verifier together
acceptance: A committed report (eval/COMBINED_CORRUPTION.md or similar) states, across all 76 real cases, how many true SEV1 retraction cases pass BOTH the confidence gate and the deterministic verifier undetected
Method is reproducible: a script under eval/ regenerates the number
Full test suite still green
constraints: Measurement task: no behavior changes to classifier or verifier
combined-corruption-rate.result: 0/76 SEV1 cases leak through both shipped layers; eval/COMBINED_CORRUPTION.md + eval/run_combined.py committed; caveats documented (gate luck, verifier circularity, 1 missed WRITE_NEW correction)

dogfood-consolidation.title: Dogfood: run consolidation on Recall's own build history
acceptance: Episodic captures exist under brain/episodic/ for the material decisions of this build (dual-representation split, executor distrust of low-confidence, 65.3% ceiling as constraint, AIW boundary)
'recall consolidate run' processes them and the review queue / semantic tier reflect the outcome
A written finding (eval/DOGFOOD_FINDINGS.md) answers: does retrieval surface 'why dual-representation' and 'why the executor distrusts low-confidence classifications' correctly?
If it does not surface them well, the finding says so plainly and is filed as a real signal, not smoothed over
constraints: Uses the real classifier (measured), not a mock; cost is small but real
Captures are append-only; do not rewrite history to make consolidation look good

phase8-polish.title: Phase 8 CLI polish: recall status + review-queue UX
acceptance: recall status prints pending review-queue count, recent consolidation activity, and last-index-build info; exits 0
review-queue interaction (list/accept/override) has consistent, readable output
recall status limitation note references retraction-limitation-doc
New tests cover recall status; full suite green

provider-portability.title: Make the write-path classifier provider-swappable
acceptance: classifier.classify() selects provider/model via a documented interface or config; Anthropic stays the default
At least one alternative provider path exists (or a clean adapter seam with a second impl) and is exercised by a test with a fake client
The RuntimeError message no longer says 'no local classifier is supported' as an absolute; it names the configured provider
eval/PHASE*_*.md or a new eval note reports MEASURED accuracy for any provider claimed to work (invariant 6); no assumed numbers
constraints: Do not change DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD or the prompt as part of this task
Invariant 6: any 'works with provider X' claim needs a measured number on eval/classifier_set/real_examples.yaml

readme-accuracy.title: README reflects the actually-implemented system state
acceptance: README Status section lists Phases 0-7 + Phase 2 follow-up + Phase 6 as done, not 'Phase 0/1'
No sentence in README claims consolidation, retrieval, injection, or verification is unimplemented
README Usage documents every command shown by 'recall --help' (capture, index build, consolidate run, review list/accept/override, retrieve, status)
Full test suite still green after the edit
constraints: Docs-only task: no changes under src/ or tests/
Do not overstate — Phase 6 is 'partial (deterministic verifier shipped, NLI evaluated and rejected)', not 'done'

argv: ! grep -nE "not implemented yet|Phase 0/1|are not implemented" README.md

readme-accuracy.result: README Status now covers Phases 0-7 + Phase 2 follow-up + Phase 6 partial; Usage documents every recall --help command; 53 pytest pass; grep check clean

argv: ! grep -nE "not implemented yet|Phase 0/1|are not implemented" README.md

recall-status-cmd.title: Implement 'recall status' (BUILD_PLAN Phase 8)
acceptance: 'recall status' exits 0 and prints: pending review-queue count, most-recent consolidation summary (or 'never run'), and whether the SQLite index is stale vs brain/
No network and no model call in the status path
New test in tests/ covers the command against a temp brain/ with 0 and >0 pending items
src/cli.py no longer contains the 'not yet implemented' stub for status
constraints: Read-only: must not trigger consolidation or index rebuild as a side effect (may read the existing index; report staleness rather than fixing it)
Honor invariant: no expensive reasoning in a read path

retraction-classifier-revisit.title: Revisit a purpose-built retraction classifier once real corrections exist
acceptance: Only startable once the correction log holds a meaningful number of real retraction-labelled examples
Either a trained/prompt-specialized retraction check that beats the current deterministic verifier on held-out real data, or a recorded decision that it still is not worth it
constraints: Do not start before real correction data exists (the whole point)

retraction-limitation-doc.title: Document the retraction blind spot (no first-person lexical signal = not caught)
acceptance: A LIMITATIONS.md (or ARCHITECTURE.md section) states plainly that the shipped verifier only catches retractions with first-person lexical cues, and cites the combined-corruption-rate number
README links to it from the Phase 6 status line
Full test suite still green
constraints: Docs task: no changes under src/ or tests/

start-daily-usage.title: Begin real daily usage of recall on actual notes/work
acceptance: brain/episodic/ contains real (non-eval, non-dogfood-of-build) captures from actual note-taking over multiple days
at least one real consolidate run has been executed on that corpus
constraints: Owner-driven: requires the user to actually use the tool; agent cannot fabricate this

stop-synthetic-eval.title: Decision: freeze hand-authored/synthetic eval-case creation
acceptance: A .ai/decisions/ entry records: stop adding synthetic/hand-authored eval cases (diminishing returns + overfitting risk); future eval signal comes from real usage corrections
recall capture --source stop-synthetic-eval records the rationale
constraints: Decision-only: no code or eval-data changes

wire-phase7-correction-log.title: Confirm Phase 7 correction log accumulates from real review actions
acceptance: A test or documented manual trace shows: running recall review accept/override on a real queue item appends a labelled example (facts_in, classification_given, confidence_given, correct_classification) to the correction log on disk
If it is only built and not wired, the gap is fixed; if already wired, the confirming test is added
Full test suite green
